sub_topics: The CBCP's demand: more than abolishing EO 464, the bishops wanted a 'determined and relentless' search for truth 'untrammeled' -- their program of 'Seeking the Truth, Restoring Integrity'
The 'symbolic act': GMA's revocation of EO 464 and Memorandum Circular 108, which Solicitor General Agnes Devanadera herself called 'symbolic,' did not satisfy the bishops' desiderata

To 'complete the joy' of the bishops, CJP urged GMA to let Romulo Neri testify freely; continuing to invoke executive privilege 'improperly in my humble view' would only deepen the perception that GMA was personally involved in the ZTE bribery

No direct link -- yet: there is no evidence directly tying GMA to the alleged overprice; neither Jun Lozada nor Joey de Venecia has said she was a direct beneficiary of the supposed '$130-million commission' -- but barring Neri fosters the belief that his testimony would link her

The three questions: whether the President (1) had any interest in the NBN project, (2) ordered Neri to prioritize it, and (3) ordered its continuance despite his bribery allegations -- questions whose negative answers would clear her, so the will to silence Neri implies the answers are positive

The cover-up inference: the insistence on secrecy 'merely fortifies' the claim of the 80 Former Senior Government Officials (FSGO) that GMA was 'at the center of the corruption and cover-up'; 'if she were innocent, why... would she prevent Neri from telling the truth?'

Senate v. Ermita and the pressure on the Court: under the unanimous Ermita ruling, Neri's plea for silence cannot be granted; reports of 'tremendous pressures' on the justices to reverse or carve exceptions are 'normal,' and CJP trusts they will decide as jurists 'knowing history will ultimately judge them'

The long view and the tipping point: the truth 'cannot be hidden forever,' so it is better it 'shine forth now' while GMA can contain the damage; the Senate and the Supreme Court are the only trusted truth-seeking institutions, and a surprise pro-secrecy ruling that abruptly halts the Senate probe could be the crisis 'tipping point' -- like the Enrile-Ramos defiance or the prosecutors' walkout -- driving the 'middle forces' to 'volcanic communal action' (a 'new type of people power,' per CBCP president Lagdameo)

one_paragraph_summary: Chapter 4 of 'With Due Respect' (Vol. 1), CJP's March 16, 2008 Inquirer column, argues that GMA's revocation of EO 464 and Memorandum Circular 108 -- which Solicitor General Devanadera herself called a 'symbolic act' -- did not satisfy the CBCP's call for a 'determined and relentless,' 'untrammeled' search for truth. To 'complete the joy' of the bishops, he urges GMA to let former NEDA chief Romulo Neri testify freely at the Senate's NBN-ZTE probe instead of invoking executive privilege. While conceding there is no evidence directly linking her to the alleged overprice -- neither Jun Lozada nor Joey de Venecia has named her a beneficiary of the supposed '$130-million commission' -- he contends that barring Neri only fosters the belief that his testimony would incriminate her. He lists the three questions GMA did not want answered (whether she had an interest in the NBN project, ordered it prioritized, or ordered it continued despite bribery allegations) and reasons that negative answers would clear her, so the will to silence Neri implies the answers are 'positive': 'if she were innocent, why... would she prevent Neri from telling the truth?' The secrecy, he says, only fortifies the claim of the 80 Former Senior Government Officials that she was 'at the center of the corruption and cover-up.' Under the unanimous 'Senate v. Ermita' ruling, Neri's plea for silence cannot be granted, and CJP trusts the justices to resist reported pressure to reverse it. But should the Court instead enable secrecy and the Senate abruptly close its probe, that could be the crisis 'tipping point' -- like the Enrile-Ramos defiance or the prosecutors' walkout -- driving the disillusioned 'middle forces' into 'volcanic communal action,' the 'new type of people power' invoked by CBCP president Lagdameo. The truth, he insists, 'cannot be hidden forever,' so it is better it shine forth now while GMA can still contain the damage.
